Welcome To Olney Infant Academy
At Olney Infant Academy, we are dedicated to fostering a culture of excellence where every child can flourish. Our goal is to ignite a passion for learning, inspiring curiosity and enthusiasm that will set our children on the path to becoming lifelong learners. We strive to create an environment where every experience fuels growth, creativity, and confidence.
We are delighted to welcome you to our website, where you can explore all that we offer and discover the vibrant learning community that makes our school so special.

PedTech
PedTech is most powerful when it is driven by pedagogy rather than devices—used with intention to deepen learning, strengthen understanding, and empower children as active participants in their own educational journeys. Central to this approach is the belief that children thrive when they have autonomy. By enabling pupils to make choices about how they learn, and by positioning them as agentic learners who can select the tools, skills, or media they use to represent their knowledge, technology becomes a means of expression rather than a constraint.
Our ethos of enhanced provision supports this beautifully. Within rich, well‑designed environments, both physical and digital, children are offered purposeful opportunities to explore, create, collaborate, and problem‑solve. Digital tools sit alongside hands‑on materials, allowing pupils to choose the medium that best matches their strengths, interests, or intentions. Whether a child records their understanding through drawing, building, coding, voice recording, photography, or mixed‑media digital storytelling, PedTech provides an additional pathway for personalised, meaningful learning.
Balance remains key. A thoughtful PedTech approach ensures that technology enhances, rather than replaces, the social interaction, imaginative play, sensory experiences, and real‑world exploration that form the foundation of early learning. By blending digital opportunities with rich provision, we foster confident, self‑regulated, and creative learners who can navigate a digital world with independence and insight—without losing the joy, curiosity, and human connection at the heart of childhood.
We have applied to be an Apple Distinguished School (ADS) and are awaiting our response. It would be a truely proud moment for us to be accepted as one of the first First Schools in the World!

Extra-Curricular Clubs
Personal Development at the Heart of Olney Infant Academy
At Olney Infant Academy, personal development sits at the very heart of everything we do. We are passionate about nurturing children who are ready to stand out, make a difference and thrive in the ever-changing world they are growing into. Guided by our values and ethos, we believe that education is about so much more than academic success. We strive to develop confident, curious, caring and resilient young people who have the skills, character and ambition to succeed both now and in the future.
Our carefully designed personal development offer provides children with rich experiences that broaden horizons, spark new interests and build essential life skills. From leadership opportunities and community involvement to wellbeing, creativity, sustainability, innovation and future aspirations, we ensure every child has the chance to discover their strengths and develop their unique talents.
Alongside this, we are incredibly proud of our extensive range of extra-curricular clubs, which provide children with exciting opportunities to explore new passions, develop confidence and build friendships. Whether learning a new skill, solving problems, expressing creativity, taking on leadership roles or simply having fun, our clubs are designed to enrich every child's school experience. We believe these opportunities help our children become well-rounded individuals who are equipped not only for their next stage of education, but for life beyond the classroom.
Explore our exciting range of clubs and opportunities below for Autumn 2026! 🌟
A welcoming space where children can slow down, relax and develop mindfulness skills. Through yoga, colouring, breathing exercises and other calm, quiet activities, children will learn strategies to support their wellbeing while building confidence, focus and resilience.
A club designed to inspire children to dream big and explore the exciting possibilities that lie ahead. Through guest visitors, hands-on activities and discussions about different jobs and professions, children will embark on a journey of exploration, inspiration and future aspirations.
Young Engineers Discovery Club (Yr 1 and 2 only)
Perfect for curious minds who love to design, build and investigate. Children will take part in exciting engineering and STEM challenges that encourage creativity, teamwork, problem-solving and a love of discovery.
The Big Questions Club
A thought-provoking club where children are encouraged to think deeply, share ideas and listen to the views of others. Through discussions, debates and problem-solving activities, children will develop confidence in expressing their opinions while exploring some of life's big questions.
Creative Constructors Club
A hands-on club for children who love building and creating. Using LEGO®, construction materials and design challenges, children will develop their imagination, resilience and teamwork skills while bringing their ideas to life.
A fun and uplifting club where children can develop their love of singing and performing. Through learning a variety of songs, children will build confidence, creativity and teamwork while experiencing the joy of making music together.
A fun and engaging club where children can challenge their minds through puzzles, board games, logic activities and team challenges. Children will develop problem-solving skills, perseverance, strategic thinking and teamwork while enjoying a variety of exciting games and brain teasers.
Our Eco Warriors Club empowers children to become champions for the environment. Through hands-on projects, wildlife activities, gardening and learning about how to live sustainably, our Eco Warriors will develop a sense of responsibility and discover how even small actions can make a big difference to the world around them.
OIA Future Innovators (Key Stage 1 only- invite) As an Apple Distinguished School, we believe technology can empower children to create, collaborate and innovate. The OIA Future Innovators Club gives Key Stage 1 pupils the opportunity to develop their digital skills through engaging iPad projects, including coding, film-making, photography, design and digital storytelling. Children will explore how technology can enhance learning, demonstrate leadership and help us continue to innovate as part of the worldwide Apple community.
Externally Led Clubs
Led by a qualified tennis coach from Olney Tennis Club, Tennis Stars Club provides children with a fun and engaging introduction to tennis. Through exciting games, skill-building activities and match play, children will develop their coordination, agility, confidence and teamwork while learning the fundamentals of the sport in a supportive and encouraging environment.
Freestyle Football Club
Delivered by the experienced coaches from Freestyle, this exciting football club provides children with the opportunity to develop their skills, confidence and love of the game in a fun and supportive environment. Through engaging training sessions, small-sided games and team challenges, children will improve their agility, coordination, teamwork and sportsmanship while enjoying being active and making new friends.
Little Lotus Art Club A creative and calming club where children can explore their imagination through a range of exciting arts and crafts activities. Through drawing, painting, collage, sculpture and mindful creative projects, children will develop their artistic skills, self-expression and confidence in a supportive and inspiring environment. Little Lotus Art Club encourages creativity, patience and pride in achievement, while providing a wonderful opportunity for children to relax, create and have fun with friends.
OIA Gymnastics Club Led by a qualified gymnastics coach, OIA Gymnastics Club provides children with the opportunity to develop strength, balance, flexibility and coordination through engaging and enjoyable gymnastics activities. Through floor work, movement challenges, stretching and skill development, children will build confidence, resilience and body awareness in a safe and supportive environment. Whether taking their very first gymnastics steps or developing existing skills, children will have the chance to shine, celebrate their achievements and discover the joy of movement while making new friends and having lots of fun.

Sports Premium
Sports Premium at Olney Infant Academy
The PE and Sport Premium is a vital government initiative designed to help primary schools enhance the quality and breadth of physical education and sporting opportunities for all pupils. At Olney Infant Academy, we use this funding strategically to inspire a lifelong love of physical activity, improve health outcomes, and develop essential skills such as teamwork, resilience, and confidence.
Through targeted investment in high-quality teaching, specialist coaching, and a diverse range of activities, we ensure every child has access to engaging and inclusive PE lessons, after-school clubs, and competitive opportunities. Our pupils participate in sports both within the curriculum and beyond—many represent local U-6 and U-7 football and rugby teams, and take part in community tennis tournaments and other events.
We are proud that participation rates in sport and physical activity at our school are exceptionally high, and this commitment is reflected in our pupils’ wellbeing. Health data shows that, on average, our children are healthier than the national average, with significantly fewer pupils classified as overweight. This demonstrates the positive impact of our approach and the effective use of Sports Premium funding.
Our goal is clear: to give every child the confidence, skills, and enthusiasm to enjoy physical activity now and in the future.

Enhanced Provision
Environments That Empower Learning
At Olney Infant Academy, we believe that how children learn is just as important as what they learn. Our learning environments are intentionally designed to function as a third teacher: carefully structured, resource-rich, and responsive, so that every child can independently show what they know in ways that feel natural, meaningful, and confidence-building.
Our classrooms are built around continuous provision: high-quality resources and learning areas that are always available and accessible. This consistency enables children to make independent choices, return to learning with confidence, and apply skills across contexts. Within this stable framework, staff thoughtfully introduce enhanced provision, ensuring that current learning is explored more deeply, revisited creatively, and developed purposefully.
Children are trusted to select resources independently and to demonstrate their understanding in ways that suit them best, whether through talk, construction, drawing, writing, problem-solving, or imaginative role play. This reflects research-informed practice, including the work of Maria Montessori, who emphasised that independence, choice, and well-prepared environments are essential for deep and sustained learning.

Choice and independence are not seen as optional extras; they are fundamental drivers of engagement, creativity, and excellence. When children are actively involved in directing their learning, they are more invested, more reflective, and more resilient.
Enhanced provision is carefully planned to ensure children can revisit prior learning as well as explore new concepts. This approach is strongly supported by cognitive science and neuroscience research, which shows that learning is strengthened when knowledge is revisited and retrieved over time. Strategies such as spaced practice and retrieval practice, first identified by Hermann Ebbinghaus and reinforced by modern neuroscience are key to moving learning into long-term memory.

By weaving NIK and FLO into our enhanced offer, children are supported to make connections, strengthen understanding, and embed learning securely over time.
Through carefully enhanced environments, high expectations, and a culture of independence, our pupils are enabled to excel, create, and engage deeply. Enhanced provision at Olney Infant Academy ensures that learning is not only accessible and inclusive, but memorable, meaningful, and truly owned by every child.

Wrap Around Care
Kidz Club
Breakfast Club
Our Breakfast Club opens from 7.45am every morning. It costs £4.50 per session. At 8.40am the children are taken to their classrooms. We serve healthy breakfasts (cereals, toast, fruit juice etc) and provide quiet activities to keep them busy. If you would like your child to use this facility, please book online via your MCAS account. Contact the office if you need assistance. We prefer to have at least a day’s notice of attendance.
After-School and Holiday Clubs
Our After-School Club runs every school day from 3 - 6 pm. It costs £12.50 per session though if your child has attended one of the extra-curricular clubs this reduces to £8.50. It is run by our school staff so they know all the children very well. Book online via your MCAS account. Please ask at the school office for further details.
We are also open from 8.15am - 5pm during most weeks of the school holidays, and closed Bank Holidays and the week between Christmas and New Year.
Both of these clubs include a wide range of games and activities both indoors and outdoors.

SEND
Special Educational Need and Disability
At OIA, provision for pupils with SEND is co-ordinated by the school SENDCo Mrs Kim Millican (Inclusion Lead)
CONTACT: Kmillican@iftl.co.uk
There are times when some children need additional support during their school life. Olney Infant Academy is an inclusive school which offers a range of additional provision to support children with various SEND: including social, communication and interaction needs, learning difficulties, emotional and mental health needs and physical needs.
We endeavour to identify promptly a child’s particular needs and respond appropriately to enable them to make progress alongside their peers.
A systematic approach is essential within school with processes in place to ensure support and continuity of provision and effective communication with parents. The Government’s ‘SEND Code of Practice (2014)’ provides the framework for these processes. The school’s SEN Policy is written to reflect Government policy in the Code of Practice.

Professional Development: Investing in Our People
At Olney Infant Academy, we believe that exceptional outcomes for children are rooted in exceptional adults. High-quality, sustained professional development (CPD) is therefore central to our school improvement journey and to ensuring our ethos is lived consistently across every classroom and learning space.
Our approach to CPD begins with shared belief. For our vision of purposeful autonomy, high expectations, and inclusive excellence to be realised, staff must genuinely buy into the ethos of the school. This is achieved not through compliance, but through professional dialogue, trust, and research-informed practice. We invest time in building a common language around learning so that our values are understood, owned, and enacted by all.

Staff regularly engage with high-quality research, professional blogs, and current thinking from the field of education. This includes insights from cognitive psychology, neuroscience, and pedagogical research, such as the importance of retrieval practice and metacognition, building on the foundational work of researchers like Hermann Ebbinghaus and modern educational neuroscience.

This layered support ensures that professional learning is contextualised, sustainable, and impact-driven. Staff are given time to reflect, trial strategies, receive feedback, and refine practice, recognising that meaningful change happens over time, not through one-off training sessions.
By grounding CPD in the most up-to-date research and aligning it closely with our ethos, we ensure that every adult at Olney Infant Academy is empowered, confident, and highly skilled. This shared commitment to professional growth directly strengthens teaching quality, learning environments, and ultimately the life chances of the children we serve.

Come And Visit Our School
"Tell me and I forget. Teach me and I remember. Involve me, and I learn." — Benjamin Franklin
Provision with Purpose Workshops
Over the past couple of years, the demand for visits has grown significantly, which is fantastic. We are always keen to say yes to visitors who are eager to join us on a journey of applying an early years‑principled approach beyond the Early Years Foundation Stage. Due to this increasing interest, we are now introducing a more structured programme of visits, welcoming guests in groups and developing these opportunities into more meaningful workshop experiences.
These sessions are no longer simply a ‘sneaky peek’ into our classrooms. Instead, they offer a deeper insight into our journey as a school; sharing our successes, being honest about the challenges we have faced, and exploring how we have evolved our provision over time.
Throughout the workshops, visitors will see how our approach develops from strong foundations in the Early Years, where a largely technology‑light environment supports language, play and interaction, into a carefully considered provision across the rest of the school. We also share how digital tools can complement learning where appropriate, always with a focus on enhancing, rather than replacing, high‑quality teaching and provision.
Workshops take place once each half term and provide opportunities to observe practice, explore purposeful learning environments, engage in professional dialogue with staff, and reflect on how these approaches could be adapted to different school contexts. These sessions are designed to be practical, collaborative and rooted in shared professional learning.
